building_envelope.caveat: the OUTER face of the external wall ring bounds this, so the envelope includes the external wall's own thickness. Free space is measured after that wall is subtracted, so a room is unaffected — but the envelope area is not a floor area
evidence: 3 ring component(s) holding 111.458 m2 of material and enclosing 1000.096 m2 — a best enclosure ratio of 38.7, which is what a ring of external wall looks like. 28 component(s) outside were NOT filled

internal_barrier_sensitivity.how_external_was_decided: a barrier lying within 1.0 mm of the envelope's own boundary closes an external opening. Membership of the wall solid's ring COMPONENT is not the test: that component carries almost every band, because internal walls touching the external ring are part of the same connected solid
internal_barrier_sensitivity.the_test: ALL vs EXTERNAL must agree to within an absolute tolerance. NONE is context and is expected to differ, because an external ring with an unclosed doorway is a C-shape rather than a ring
internal_barrier_sensitivity.why_it_matters: a barrier inside the building cannot add or remove floor. If removing the internal ones moves the envelope, the envelope is being derived from internal geometry and every area measured against it is wrong by an amount nobody can see

grid_actually_used.why: a grid smaller than the noise floor leaves coincident nodes unmerged, which shows up as spurious components in the wall solid. A grid larger than the noise floor is safe only while it stays below the nearest thing anybody drew, and the measured empty band is what establishes that

numerical_snap_tolerance.not_a_drawing_constant: this is a measurement of THIS drawing's coordinates. It is recorded per run and must not be promoted to a project or engine default: the next sheet is produced by different software with different precision
numerical_snap_tolerance.snapping_is_not_gap_closing: the recommendation sits at the representation-noise floor. A gap larger than that is two walls that do not meet, and closing it would invent material
numerical_snap_tolerance.why: 235 vertex pairs from different rings lie within 1.0 mm of each other. The largest of them is 0.00869592 mm, the population reaches <=0.01 mm, and every decade from <=0.1 mm up to the 1.0 mm ceiling is EMPTY — a clear band with nothing in it. So representation noise on this drawing ends at <=0.01 mm and the nearest thing anybody drew is at least 0.1 mm away. The grid goes at 0.01 mm: large enough to merge the coincident nodes, orders of magnitude too small to close anything drawn
numerical_snap_tolerance.why_the_measured_grid_for_production: topology, not area, decides whether a tolerance is safe. A microscopic change can still create a connection, so the established solid is built on the measured noise floor and physical junctions are closed by an explicit JUNCTION_PATCH
